cells.tense: You're here with your hands in it, and you know what you're doing.
cells.ask: offer the next one freely, without holding on to how it turns out.
cells.core: In the part of you that holds, tending well looks like this: you give what's needed and then you step back and let the thing grow at its own speed. You stand through the slow middle without leaving. You keep the conditions steady instead of checking on them every hour. The holding is real, and it doesn't take your footing out from under you. People can lean on you and you stay upright while they do.\n\nWhat keeps it clean is that nothing is being asked back. The tending is yours and the outcome isn't, so release costs nothing — the letting go is just the natural end of the job, not a loss you brace against. Offer the next thing the same way and the room to offer again shows up on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what's growing and you don't have to hold on to it.
cells.place: in the part of you that holds and keeps holding

cells.tense: You're already out ahead of a future that hasn't arrived, and both arms are full of it.
cells.ask: let one uncertain thing stay unsolved today and take the next small step anyway.
cells.core: When this part of you is working, you hold what's in front of you and let the rest wait its turn. You give the seed its water and leave the harvest alone. People can lean on you without you tipping. The strength is in what you can bear, not in what you can prevent.\n\nThat's flipped. The care has tightened into managing — everyone you tend has turned into a problem to get ahead of before it breaks — and the more you grip, the more of it lands on you alone. The holding meant to protect them is wearing you through. You can't see the ending and you don't have to. You know enough for today's move. Let the one thing that won't resolve sit unresolved, and step anyway.
cells.sheetLine: Taking care of everyone has become carrying all of them.
cells.place: in the part of you that holds and keeps holding

cells.tense: You set it down a while back, and you're still standing in the same spot.
cells.ask: point your attention at one thing you'd actually like to see grow, and give it a first small tending.
cells.core: Good tending in this part of you means staying close to something over time — not gripping it, just showing up with the water. It's steady and unspectacular and it works. You keep faith with a small thing long enough that it changes, and the change is yours. That patience is the whole capacity, and it lives here in the part of you that endures.\n\nNone of that is running. The care that used to come out of you went quiet and stayed quiet, and calling that independence doesn't change the fact that nothing is being grown. There's something you'd want to see thrive if you let yourself want it. Don't argue your way there. Turn toward it, small, and watch what answer it gives.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped tending anything, and you call the emptiness independence.
cells.place: in the part of you that holds and keeps holding

cells.tense: The hands are already moving — and no one, including you, has called it anything.
cells.ask: name one thing done as caretaking and decide whether it's really yours to hold.
cells.core: Done well in this part of you, care is a steady act — you hold people while they need it and you set them down when they don't. It's deliberate and it has a shape. You choose where the strength goes instead of spending it wherever it's asked for.\n\nWhat's happening instead is that people arrive needing something and you hold them, but the choice never registers. The role got handed over somewhere and never got put back, so no credit lands — not from them and not from you. More tiredness is riding along than gets said. Claim one piece out loud, this one is on purpose, and it becomes something you can decide about instead of something you carry.
cells.sheetLine: You're caretaking on autopilot and claiming none of it.
cells.place: in the part of you that holds and keeps holding
